slides.heading: else Statements
slides.body: else Statements is part of Conditional Execution. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: else Statements
slides.body: An else block runs when the if condition is False. It gives the program a backup path.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: else is like having Plan B. If Plan A does not happen, Plan B is followed.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: A conditional needs a colon, correct indentation, and a condition that clearly evaluates to True or False.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Use if-else to print Adult if age is at least 18, otherwise Minor.

quiz.prompt_text: When does the else block run in an if-else statement?

options: When the if condition is True
Only when there is an error
When the if condition is False

quiz.explanation: Correct! The else block is the backup path. It runs only when the if condition is False.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines to print Passed if score is at least 75, otherwise Try again.
quiz.explanation: score is assigned, then the if block, then the else block. Python only runs else when the if condition is False.

quiz.prompt_text: Use if-else to print Adult if age is at least 18, otherwise print Minor.

content.hint: Use if age >= 18: then else: with their indented print lines.

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: With age = 16, the else block runs and prints Minor. The else provides a response for every path not covered by the if.
